title: Utah's toughest grid days
note: illustrative case study; validation days only; from the registered run's ledgers (no new simulation); not part of the registered experiment
rule: D-066 (pre-registered before any day was examined): the top 3 validation days (America/Denver dates in [2024-11-01, 2025-10-24)) by PACE daily maximum hourly net load (EIA-930 adjusted demand, isolated spikes removed, minus wind and solar); ties go to the earlier date; each day's rank is reported; no day is ever substituted
accounting: day-sliced accounting: execution energy counted in the hour it ran (exact overlap with each UTC hour of the local day) at the execution site's hourly intensity; transfer energy at its arrival hour, half at home and half at the destination (F14.5). A job spanning midnight is split between days. Summed over every hour of the cohort window, it equals the registered accounting

accounting_check.rule: Σ over every hour of the cohort window of hourly kWh × hourly intensity equals Σ execution_co2_kg of the registered job accounting (rel 1e-9)

hour_index: index i of every hourly series is the i-th hour of the local (America/Denver) day, starting at local midnight
weather_note: descriptive context only: it never feeds any model or decision. Archived forecast products (Open-Meteo, CC BY 4.0), so labelled forecast; daily max and min over the hourly instants of the local day; degree days from the mean of max and min, base 65 °F. Salt Lake City is the only PACE load-centre point in the archive; Milford and Medicine Bow are resource sites, not load-weighted
context_note: context, not evidence for any result: public sources found for each date (accessed 27 Oct 2026); no cause is inferred beyond the source
